parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish فلوقه (fıluka, fılıka, füluka, filuka), فولوقه (fuluka), فلكه, فلیكه (filika), from Arabic فَلُوكَة (falūka), partially via Italian feluca, from Arabic فُلْك (fulk).

From Ottoman Turkish قرصان (korsan, “pirate”), from Arabic قُرْصَان (qurṣān, “pirate”), from Italian corsale (“corsair, privateer”), from Medieval Latin cursārius (“pirate, sea-raider”), from Latin cursus (“course, a running; plunder, hostile inroad”). Doublet of kurs and kur.
